chains.title: T allele strengthens a GATA site in the TOX3 enhancer; GATA3, which occupies this element in MCF7, mediates the effect

links.claim: The GATA specificity group passes the screen with all 6 models agreeing the alt (T) allele binds more (best model GATA2 z 18.65, effect +0.283; site strength 92.3th to 98.6th percentile). Within the group I pick GATA3 because it is by far the most expressed member in MCF7 (346 TPM vs GATA2 12.7, rest <1), has its own QBiC-SELEX model, and is the only group member with direct ChIP-seq occupancy at this variant: 5 ENCODE GATA3 peaks in MCF-7 and further peaks in T47D and A549 contain chr16:52565276. The direction (alt stronger) is a group-level in vitro prediction, not measured allele-specific binding.

The variant lies in dELS cCRE EH38E3180851 (DNase z 4.2, H3K27ac z 6.1; maxima across biosamples) and in Ensembl enhancer ENSR16_9QTBS; GATA3 ChIP peaks in MCF-7 show the element is bound in the relevant cell line.

The cCRE is assigned to CASC16/TOX3; TOX3 is 17.5 kb away and the top L2G gene (0.92-0.96) in breast cancer credible sets where the variant has PIP 1.00. No breast eQTL supports this link (0 significant GTEx breast eQTLs), so the gene assignment rests on proximity and L2G only, and CASC16 is not excluded.

The element is occupied by GATA3 in MCF-7 and T47D (both luminal breast lines), matching the MCF7 expression context; associations are reported for both ER+ and ER- breast cancer, so I do not claim subtype specificity.

If allelic GATA3 binding changes enhancer output onto TOX3, this would alter breast cancer risk in T-allele carriers; the T allele is the risk allele in the largest studies, but the direction of the TOX3 expression change is not established by any cited evidence.

chains.title: T allele strengthens a FOXA1 (forkhead) site in the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: The FOXA1 lookup shows its own QBiC-SELEX model passes the gate with the alt allele binding more (effect +0.314, z 9.34, rank 82/997; site strength 99.0th to 99.8th percentile), and the CIS-BP FOXA2 model agrees (effect +0.296, z 15.4). Direction is alt-stronger, but the effect size is small relative to the Maf and GATA groups, and no FOXA1 ChIP evidence at this element is in the evidence set.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE / Ensembl enhancer, the class of element FOXA1 pioneers in breast cells; no FOXA1 occupancy at this cCRE is shown in the cited data.
The enhancer is assigned to CASC16/TOX3 and TOX3 is the top L2G gene; no contact or eQTL evidence links the element to TOX3 in breast.

The QBiC lookup was run in the MCF7 expression context, which the screen uses for a 1 TPM expression filter, and FOXA1 was returned as a scored, gated model; direct FOXA1 TPM in MCF7 is not quoted here.

Greater pioneer-factor binding on the T allele could open the enhancer further and alter TOX3 levels, matching the T-allele risk association; no cited evidence connects FOXA1 to TOX3 levels at this variant.

chains.title: T allele creates a strong small-Maf (MAFK/MAFG) site that rewires the enhancer

links.claim: The small-Maf group gives the largest effect in the screen (best model MAFG z 71.57, effect +2.788; alt site strength 100th vs ref 97.6th percentile), with all 6 models alt-stronger. I pick MAFK because it is the most expressed small Maf in MCF7 (16.96 TPM vs MAFG 8.48) and has its own model and a passing z of 48.84; the choice rests on expression alone, with no ChIP support.
The predicted gained site falls inside an active distal enhancer-like cCRE with high H3K27ac (maxima across biosamples).
The cCRE is assigned to CASC16/TOX3 and TOX3 is the top L2G gene; no eQTL in breast supports a TOX3 link.
MAFK and MAFG are expressed above 1 TPM in MCF7, so a created MARE could in principle be bound there; occupancy is unverified.
If bound, small Mafs could repress (as homodimers) or activate (with CNC partners), changing TOX3 output; no cited evidence ties Maf factors to this locus or to risk, so this step is unsupported.

chains.title: C (ref) allele preferentially binds NFAT; loss of NFATC3 binding on the T allele changes enhancer output

links.claim: The Rel/NFAT group passes with all three models ref-stronger (best model NFATC4 z -23.46, effect -1.044; site strength 98.0th to 70.9th percentile). I pick NFATC3 as the most expressed member in MCF7 (9.54 TPM) and a passing own-model member, though its own z (-4.28) is barely above the gate and the best model belongs to a low-expressed paralogue.
The predicted lost site lies within the dELS cCRE containing the variant.
TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and the top L2G target; no breast eQTL supports the link.
NFATC3 is expressed in MCF7, so a ref-specific site could be occupied in luminal breast cells; occupancy is not shown.
A change in NFAT occupancy between alleles could alter enhancer output and TOX3 levels; the direction of that change and its link to risk are not supported by cited evidence.

grades_v0.reason: E17 shows the GATA group passes with consistent alt-stronger direction, but the best model is GATA2 and the GATA3 own-model row is not shown. This is a prediction only, and picking GATA3 by TPM is a reasoned but untested choice. No ChIP or allelic data.

E03 places the variant in dELS cCRE EH38E3180851 with H3K27ac z 6.1 and DNase z 4.2, and E01 gives an Ensembl enhancer. These are maxima over biosamples, so MCF7 activity is not shown, which limits it to epigenomic context.

E05 gives L2G for TOX3 of 0.92-0.96 with PIP 1.00 for the variant, and E02 gives proximity (17.5 kb). This is genetic and proximity support only; no eQTL, CRISPR or contact data link this enhancer to TOX3. Brain TOX3 tuQTLs have low PIP.

GATA3 at 346 TPM in MCF7 (E17) and ER+/luminal credible sets (E05) fit. The ER+ versus ER- effect-size claim is not shown: E04 lists ER- p 2e-26 against ER+ p 1e-13 in a different cohort. No cell-type-specific enhancer activity evidence is given.

The T-allele risk association is strong (E04) and E06a/E06b support enhancer/TOX3 and T-allele risk. Nothing shows GATA3-dependent TOX3 change or luminal differentiation effects; the mechanism is over-claimed. Direction of TOX3 expression change is unspecified.

FOXA1 is not in any screen group row and was not looked up. The claim that the T allele binds more is not backed by any quoted evidence; E06a mentions TOX3 enhancer but not FOXA1. Coverage is marked not_checked.
The cCRE and enhancer annotation (E01/E03) is real, but it says nothing about FOXA1 occupancy or a FOXA1 motif at the site.
TOX3 L2G and the E06a enhancer-mutation quote support TOX3 as the gene, as for the other chains. There is no looping evidence despite 'loops to TOX3' being asserted.
No cited evidence shows FOXA1 expression in MCF7 or ER+ cells; E04 and E05 only give GWAS/credible-set data. FOXA1 TPM was not retrieved.
The risk association is solid (E04/E06b), but nothing links FOXA1 to TOX3 levels or risk at this variant.

E08 shows a very large alt-stronger effect, with all 6 models concordant, for the Maf group. However, it is a prediction only. MAFK is chosen by TPM among members, and the best model is MAFG; the 'MARE-like site' is unverified.
The variant sits in an active dELS cCRE (E03) and an Ensembl enhancer (E01); biosample-specific signal for MCF7 is not shown.
The TOX3 L2G and proximity evidence (E02, E03, E05) is genetic or positional only, with no regulatory link demonstrated.
E08 gives MAFK 16.96 TPM and MAFG 8.48 TPM in MCF7, so expression is supported, but expression does not show occupancy in vivo.
The activator or repressor role is left open, so the effect direction on TOX3 is not committed. E04/E06a say nothing about Maf factors, so the chain from binding to risk is unsupported.

E11 shows NFAT group ref-stronger, which is directionally consistent. NFATC3 is a weaker passing member (z -4.28, barely above the gate), while the best is NFATC4 at 0.86 TPM. The TF choice rests on TPM alone and no ChIP evidence is cited.
The variant lies within the dELS cCRE (E03/E01); same caveat on biosample specificity.
TOX3 is the nearest gene and top L2G (E02/E05), which is genetic and proximity support only.
NFATC3 at 9.54 TPM shows it is expressed in MCF7, but there is no evidence that it occupies this site. Cell-type relevance to breast risk is not shown.

Claims of de-repression and increased risk via NFAT loss are not supported by any cited evidence. The title says de-repression, while the phenotype step says altered regulation; the direction of the TOX3 effect is unsupported.

grades_final.reason: Group-level QBiC prediction (alt stronger, all 6 GATA models agree) plus GATA3 ChIP peaks containing the variant in MCF-7. The ChIP shows occupancy but not allele-specific binding. The choice of GATA3 is justified by TPM, own model, and ChIP. Still a prediction plus context, not perturbation.

The variant lies in cCRE EH38E3180851 (dELS) and in Ensembl enhancer ENSR16_9QTBS, with H3K27ac z 6.1 and DNase z 4.2. GATA3 ChIP peaks in MCF-7 contain it. Biosample-specific z-scores are not shown (maxima only), but the epigenomic overlap is direct.

TOX3 is the top L2G gene (0.92-0.96) and is 17.5 kb away, but no eQTL (0 breast GTEx), contact or perturbation data link the element to TOX3. CASC16 is not excluded. Genetic and proximity support only.

GATA3 peaks in MCF-7 and T47D support a luminal breast context, but there is no allele-specific or perturbation evidence in the cell type. The ER+/ER- claim is appropriately hedged. Only indirect occupancy context.

The T allele is associated with breast cancer (GWAS p 2e-240, PIP 1.00), and the literature quotes assert an enhancer/TOX3 link. No evidence shows the direction of the TOX3 expression change or that GATA3 mediates it. The chain is conditional ('if'), and the quotes are reviews/meta-analysis, not functional data.
The FOXA1 own model passes the gate with alt stronger (E19, z 9.34, effect +0.314), and the FOXA2 model agrees. This is a QBiC prediction alone with a small effect, and no FOXA1 ChIP is cited.
The variant lies in an enhancer-like cCRE, but no FOXA1 occupancy is shown there. The pioneer-factor claim rests on general knowledge, not the cited evidence.
TOX3 is the top L2G gene and nearby, but there is no eQTL or contact evidence (0 breast eQTLs). Proximity and genetics only.

FOXA1 expression in MCF7 is not quoted, and the claim only says the model was scored in the MCF7 context. The screen's 1 TPM filter is not shown to apply to FOXA1 here. There is no FOXA1 occupancy or expression evidence in breast cells. Suggest looking up FOXA1 TPM and ChIP in MCF-7.
The GWAS association supports a locus-level phenotype, but no cited evidence connects FOXA1 to TOX3 levels or risk at this variant. The claim is speculative.

The small-Maf group gives a very large alt-stronger prediction (MAFG z 71.57), and MAFK has an own model with passing z 48.84. MAFK was chosen on expression alone, with no ChIP or perturbation support. Prediction only.
The variant lies in an active enhancer-like cCRE (H3K27ac z 6.1, maxima across biosamples), but no Maf occupancy is shown there. Context only.
TOX3 is the top L2G gene and nearby, but there is no breast eQTL or contact evidence. Proximity and genetics only.
MAFK (16.96 TPM) and MAFG (8.48 TPM) are expressed in MCF7, so binding is possible. Occupancy is unverified, and expression is the only support.
No evidence is cited, and the chain admits that the step is unsupported. The repress/activate direction is undetermined.

The Rel/NFAT group has 3 models with ref stronger, so the direction is consistent. NFATC3's own z (-4.28) barely passes the gate, and the best model belongs to NFATC4 (0.86 TPM). NFATC3 was chosen on expression alone. Prediction only and marginal.
The variant lies in the dELS cCRE, but there is no NFAT occupancy evidence. Context only.
TOX3 is nearest and top L2G, but there is no breast eQTL or contact support. The claim is proximity and genetics only.
NFATC3 is expressed at 9.54 TPM in MCF7, but occupancy is not shown. Expression context only.
The claim acknowledges that the direction and link to risk are unsupported. The GWAS cites the locus, not NFAT. The T allele loses binding, but no evidence ties this to risk.
